title: AI Agents for Tax Resolution: A Workflow Guide
summary: Learn where AI agents can help tax resolution teams prepare collection forms, review financial records, and research IRM guidance with human oversight.
body_markdown:
An AI agent is useful when it helps move a defined task from source material to a reviewable draft. For tax resolution teams, that might mean reading a client’s bank statements and intake records, mapping financial figures into an IRS collection form, or locating relevant Internal Revenue Manual (IRM) sections. It is not a substitute for the enrolled agent or case manager.


## Start with the case, not the model


A collection case involves records from different places: statements, tax transcripts, intake forms, and supporting documents. Before asking an agent to prepare anything, identify the form and the period under review. Rima’s[document automation](https://www.getrima.ai/product/document-automation) supports preparation of 433-F, 433-B, and 433-A (OIC) from financial documents. It maps values to form fields and flags missing or inconsistent information for a case manager to check. Rima also supports[1040 preparation](https://www.getrima.ai/who-we-serve) from source documents, with professional review before final decisions.


## Keep research and advocacy reviewable


Rima[Advisor](https://www.getrima.ai/product/advisor) helps evaluate a resolution path, identify possible advocacy angles, and surface supporting IRM sections. A citation is a starting point for review, not an automatic legal conclusion. Practitioners should verify the section, the client facts, and the applicable standards before relying on an argument.


## Give each step a human owner


- **Intake:** confirm the documents belong to the right client and period.
- **Preparation:** check extracted amounts against source pages and resolve gaps.
- **Review:** assess proposed form entries and advocacy in the context of the entire case.
- **Approval:** keep the final submission decision with the responsible professional.


For a narrow starting point, consider a single collection-form workflow. The[433-F case study](https://www.getrima.ai/resources/case-study/433-f-prep) describes one firm’s preparation process moving from about 90 minutes to 30 minutes. That observation should not be treated as a universal result for every case or form.


Related reading:[document processing for accountants](https://www.getrima.ai/blog/ai-document-processing-accountants) and[how to evaluate automation ROI](https://www.getrima.ai/blog/tax-resolution-firm-roi) .
